documents.title: History and Physical - Admission
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time seen: 21:40, ED bay 4
Chief complaint: shortness of breath and leg swelling x 1 week
HPI:
67 yo male with known HFrEF (EF 30% by echo 8 months ago), HTN, CKD stage 3, T2DM, presents with progressive dyspnea.
Symptoms began roughly 10 days ago with orthopnea, now sleeping on 3 pillows, up from 1.
Reports shortness of breath climbing one flight of stairs; comfortable at rest.
Two episodes of PND in the last 3 nights. No chest pain. No fever, no cough productive of sputum.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Denies dietary indiscretion but admits to canned soup and deli meat several times last week.
No recent travel, no leg pain, no hemoptysis.
Reports new palpitations starting yesterday evening, intermittent, lasting minutes at a time.
ED course: SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%.
Furosemide 40 mg IV given once in the ED with good urine output; 900 mL in the first 2 hours.
PMH:
HFrEF, ischemic cardiomyopathy, prior anterior MI with PCI to LAD
Hypertension
CKD stage 3
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hyperlipidemia
Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 12 years ago
Home meds:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID
Carvedilol 12.5 mg PO BID
Sacubitril-valsartan 49/51 mg PO BID
Spironolactone 25 mg PO daily
Empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
Aspirin 81 mg PO daily
Allergies: NKDA
Social: lives with wife, one flight of stairs to bedroom, independent in ADLs. No alcohol.
Family hx: father MI age 60.
ROS: per HPI, otherwise negative. No urinary symptoms, no melena.
Physical Exam:
Vitals 21:45 - T 36.8, HR 138, BP 108/74, respiratory rate 20, SpO2 91% on 4L NC
Gen: elderly male, mildly dyspneic with speech in full sentences, no accessory muscle use
HEENT: JVP elevated to angle of jaw at 45 degrees
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, tachycardic, no appreciable murmur, S3 difficult to assess given rate
Lungs: bibasilar crackles to mid lung fields bilaterally, decreased breath sounds at both bases
Abd: soft, mild RUQ fullness, no tenderness
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid thigh bilaterally, warm, pulses 2+
Neuro: alert and oriented x3, nonfocal
Data:
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago).
Na 134, K 4.2, CO2 24, BUN 42, glucose 168
Troponin 0.04 ng/mL, flat on repeat at 0.04
WBC 7.8, Hgb 12.6, Plt 210
ECG 21:50: irregularly irregular narrow complex tachycardia at 138, no acute ST changes, old anteroseptal Q waves
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
Assessment/Plan:
67 yo male with acute decompensated HFrEF, volume overloaded despite outpatient diuretic uptitration.
1. CHF exacerbation - IV diuresis, strict I/O, daily standing weights, 2 g sodium and 1.5 L fluid restriction.
2. New atrial fibrillation with RVR, heart rate 138; started diltiazem drip; on continuous telemetry.
Rate likely contributing to decompensation. Hold carvedilol uptitration until drip weaned. CHA2DS2-VASc reviewed, anticoag to be discussed.
3. Acute on chronic kidney injury - likely cardiorenal. Hold sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone for now, trend BMP daily.
4. Hypoxemia - continue 4L NC, wean as able, target SpO2 >92%.
5. DM - hold home regimen, SSI while inpatient.
Admit to telemetry, cardiology consulted.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:20
Subjective: Pt reports breathing better overnight. Slept on 2 pillows. No chest pain. Up to bathroom twice with RN assist.
Still notes leg heaviness. Appetite fair.
Overnight events: diltiazem drip titrated to 12.5 mg/hr at 01:30 for HR 124. Rates 88-104 since 03:00.
Urine output 2,150 mL since midnight, 3,400 mL total since admission.
Weight down 1.2 kg from admission.
Objective:
T 36.6, HR 96 irregular, BP 102/66, RR 18, SpO2 92%
Remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
Gen: comfortable, conversant in full sentences
Cardiac: irregularly irregular, rate controlled
Lungs: crackles now at bases only, improved from admission
Ext: 2+ pitting edema to knees, improved
Labs this AM: Creatinine 2.4 mg/dL on hospital day 2, Na 135, K 3.8, BUN 46
Assessment/Plan:
1. Acute decompensated HFrEF - responding to diuresis. Furosemide 40 mg IV given once in the ED with good urine output; switched to home oral dose the next morning.
Restart furosemide 80 mg PO BID this AM, recheck I/O this afternoon.
2. Atrial fibrillation - rate improved on drip. Plan transition to oral diltiazem later today if HR stays <110.
Anticoagulation discussed with cardiology, apixaban to start pending renal trend.
3. AKI on CKD - creatinine up, likely diuresis related vs cardiorenal. Continue to hold sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone. Repeat BMP this PM.
4. Hypoxemia - attempt wean to 2L this afternoon if ambulatory sats hold.
5. Replete K to goal >4.0. KCl 40 mEq PO x1.
Continue daily weights, strict I/O, 1.5 L fluid restriction.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 16:05 - interval note
Subjective: Pt sitting up in chair, ate most of lunch. Denies dyspnea at rest. Ambulated 60 feet in hallway with RN.
Notes mild lightheadedness when standing quickly, resolved on sitting.
Interval events: diltiazem drip off at 13:40, transitioned to diltiazem 120 mg PO daily.
Took first oral furosemide 80 mg at 08:30, 1,100 mL out in the following 4 hours.
Objective:
14:50 vitals: HR 92 irregular, BP 106/70, RR 18, SpO2 93% on 2L NC
Ambulatory sats 90% on 2L NC over 60 feet, recovered to 94% at rest after 2 min.
Telemetry: atrial fibrillation, rates 84-106, no pauses, no ventricular ectopy runs.
Net negative 1,850 mL for the day so far. Total net negative 4,100 mL.
Weight 2.6 kg below admission weight.
Lungs: scattered bibasilar crackles, no wheeze
Ext: 2+ edema to mid shin, continued improvement
PM BMP: creatinine 2.3, K 4.1, Na 136, BUN 44
Assessment/Plan:
1. CHF - continued good response to oral diuretic. Continue furosemide 80 mg PO BID.
2. Afib - rate controlled off drip. Continue oral diltiazem, telemetry overnight. Apixaban 5 mg BID started at 16:00 per cardiology.
3. AKI - creatinine stable to slightly improved this PM. Recheck AM.
4. O2 - weaned to 2L NC, trial off overnight if sats permit.
5. Cardiac rehab and heart failure education consult placed; daily weight log reviewed with pt and wife.
Anticipate discharge tomorrow if renal function stable and off supplemental O2.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Length of stay: 3 days. Discharged HD3 at 14:15.
Discharge diagnoses:
1. Acute on chronic decompensated systolic heart failure (HFrEF, EF 30%)
2. New atrial fibrillation with RVR
3. Acute kidney injury on CKD stage 3
4. Hypoxemic respiratory insufficiency, resolved
Brief hospital course:
67 yo male with HFrEF presented with 10 days of progressive dyspnea, orthopnea and leg swelling.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
On arrival SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Chest x-ray: diffuse bilateral interstitial opacities with cephalization and moderate bilateral effusions, increased from prior study.
Furosemide 40 mg IV given once in the ED with good urine output; switched to home oral dose the next morning.
New atrial fibrillation with RVR, heart rate 138; started diltiazem drip; on continuous telemetry. Drip weaned HD2 and converted to oral diltiazem.
Apixaban started HD2 after discussion with cardiology.
Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago), 2.4 mg/dL on hospital day 2. Down to 1.9 mg/dL on HD3.
Total net negative 5,600 mL; weight down 4.0 kg from admission.
Oxygen weaned to room air HD3 at 09:00, ambulatory sat 93% on RA over 150 feet.
Discharge exam: HR 84 irregular, BP 110/68, respiratory rate 20, SpO2 93% RA, trace ankle edema, lungs clear to bases.
Reports shortness of breath climbing one flight of stairs; comfortable at rest.
Discharge medications:
Furosemide 80 mg PO BID
Diltiazem ER 120 mg PO daily
Apixaban 5 mg PO BID
Carvedilol 12.5 mg PO BID
Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily
Empagliflozin 10 mg PO daily
Sacubitril-valsartan and spironolactone held at discharge, to be resumed by cardiology once creatinine stable.
Instructions: daily weights same time each morning, call for gain >2 kg in 3 days. 2 g sodium diet, 1.5 L fluid limit.
Follow-up: heart failure clinic in 5 days with BMP; cardiology in 2 weeks for rhythm and anticoagulation review.
Return precautions: worsening dyspnea, chest pain, syncope, bleeding, weight gain, or decreased urine output.
